No photo shows the camera powered on, a live LCD image, or a test shot.
No screenshot of the camera's shutter-count menu or EXIF data from a test image.

risks.risk: Camera may not power on or may have sensor/shutter faults
risks.proof: Short video of camera powering on, taking a shot, and displaying it on the LCD

risks.risk: Shutter count could be much higher than claimed, affecting mechanical lifespan
risks.proof: Photo of the in-camera menu shutter count screen or a freshly shot image's EXIF data

risks.risk: Lens may have fungus, haze, or scratches on internal elements
risks.proof: Close-up photos of front and rear lens elements with a flashlight shone through at an angle

risks.risk: LCD screen could be cracked, dead-pixeled, or dim
risks.proof: Photo of the screen powered on showing a live image or menu

risks.risk: Battery/charger may be aftermarket or missing, affecting bundle value
risks.proof: Photo of battery and charger showing Canon branding/model numbers

risks.risk: Body may have hidden repair or replaced parts (not 'never repaired')
risks.proof: Photos of screw heads/seals for tamper marks, and serial number matching any warranty/service sticker

proof_requests: Video of the camera powering on, focusing, and firing the shutter with a resulting image shown on screen
Photo of the in-camera shutter count menu or EXIF data from a fresh shot
Close-up photos of front and rear lens elements lit from an angle to check for fungus/haze/scratches
Photo of the LCD screen powered on
Photo of the battery and charger showing Canon branding and model numbers
response.reason: The camera model and kit lens are clearly identified from the body and lens markings, so it can be priced at worst case (unverified function, unverified lens/shutter condition, unverified accessories) pending the listed proofs.
